title: Typeform vs Formbricks
comparison_markdown:
# Typeform vs Formbricks (2026)

## Overview
Typeform and Formbricks are both online form and survey tools used to collect data from users. This comparison benefits individuals and businesses looking to switch from a proprietary solution like Typeform to a self-hosted, open-source alternative like Formbricks. The core use case for both tools is creating and sharing forms, and someone would switch to take advantage of Formbricks' data ownership and cost savings.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Typeform offers a free plan and several paid tiers, while Formbricks is free and open-source, with costs limited to self-hosting.
* Data ownership: Formbricks allows users to retain full ownership of their data, while Typeform's terms of service grant the company certain rights to user data.
* Setup complexity: Typeform is generally easier to set up and use, with a more user-friendly interface, while Formbricks requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Formbricks can be more scalable than Typeform, since users can host it on their own servers and adjust resources as needed.
* Integration with CRM systems: Typeform has native integrations with several popular CRM systems, while Formbricks requires more custom setup and integration.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Typeform | Formbricks |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $25-$83/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $25-$40/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $100-$200/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Typeform:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Native integrations with popular CRM systems
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data ownership
* Costs can add up for large teams
**Formbricks:**
* Free and open-source
* Full control over data ownership
* Scalable and customizable
* Requires technical expertise to self-host
* Limited native integrations with CRM systems

## When to Choose Each
Typeform is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams who need a user-friendly form and survey tool with good customer support. It's also a good option for teams who don't require full control over their data and are willing to pay for the convenience of a proprietary solution. Formbricks, on the other hand, is a good choice for larger teams or organizations who require full control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and customizing their form and survey tool.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a self-hosted instance of Formbricks on your own server.
3. Use the Formbricks import tool to import your Typeform data.
4. Customize and configure your Formbricks instance as needed.
5. Test and deploy your new Formbricks instance.

## Our Take
Formbricks is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires significant technical expertise to self-host and customize. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Formbricks currently lacks native integrations with popular CRM systems, requiring custom setup and integration. However, for teams who require full control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and customizing their form and survey tool, Formbricks is a good choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams who don't need native CRM integrations and want to save on costs
* Medium-sized teams who require full control over their data and are willing to invest in self-hosting
* Large organizations who need a scalable and customizable form and survey tool
* Teams who don't need advanced analytics or reporting features
* Developers who want a self-hosted, open-source solution with full control over customization

## FAQ
### Can I use Formbricks for free?
Yes, Formbricks is free and open-source, with costs limited to self-hosting.
### Is Formbricks as easy to use as Typeform?
No, Formbricks requires more technical expertise to self-host and customize.
### Can I integrate Formbricks with my CRM system?
Yes, but it requires custom setup and integration, as Formbricks currently lacks native integrations.
### How do I migrate my data from Typeform to Formbricks?
You can export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format and use the Formbricks import tool to import it.
### Is Formbricks production-ready?
Not yet, as it requires significant technical expertise to self-host and customize.

title: Miro vs Excalidraw
comparison_markdown:
# Miro vs Excalidraw

## Overview

Online collaborative whiteboard platform. is a popular proprietary tool in the design space. Excalidraw is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Miro costs Free / $8-$16/user/month; Excalidraw is Free
- **License**: Miro is Proprietary; Excalidraw is MIT
- **Data ownership**: Excalidraw can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Excalidraw eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Excalidraw has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Miro | Excalidraw |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $8-$16/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Miro

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Excalidraw

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [excalidraw/excalidraw](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw) * ~90k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Miro if:** Miro is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Excalidraw if:** Excalidraw is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Miro in its standard export format, review Excalidraw import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Excalidraw is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Miro tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Excalidraw instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Miro, switching to self-hosted Excalidraw will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Miro until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Miro paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Excalidraw free to use?
Yes. Excalidraw is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Miro to Excalidraw?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Miro data, follow the Excalidraw import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Excalidraw get regular updates?
Yes. Excalidraw has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Excalidraw without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Excalidraw development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Miro](https://miro.com) and [Excalidraw](https://excalidraw.com) before making decisions.*

# Netlify vs Coolify (2026)

## Overview
Netlify and Coolify are two popular tools for building, deploying, and managing modern web applications. This comparison is beneficial for developers, startups, and businesses looking to switch from a proprietary platform to a self-hosted solution or seeking more control over their data. The core use case for both tools is to provide a seamless development-to-production experience, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more flexibility and autonomy.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Netlify offers a free plan with limited features, while Coolify is completely free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Coolify allows users to retain full ownership of their data, whereas Netlify stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Netlify is generally easier to set up, with a more user-friendly interface, while Coolify requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Netlify provides automatic scaling, while Coolify requires manual configuration.
* Integration: Netlify has built-in support for AWS Lambda, while Coolify supports Docker containers.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Netlify | Coolify |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $19-$99/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $19-$99/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $99-$499/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Netlify:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Automatic scaling and deployment
* Built-in support for AWS Lambda
* Large community and documentation
* Limited control over data and infrastructure
**Coolify:**
* Self-hosted and free
* Full control over data and infrastructure
* Customizable and extensible
* Supports Docker containers
* Steeper learning curve and more complex setup

## When to Choose Each
Netlify is suitable for small to medium-sized teams or individuals who prioritize ease of use and don't require fine-grained control over their infrastructure. It's ideal for projects that need to scale quickly and have built-in support for popular services like AWS Lambda. On the other hand, Coolify is a better fit for larger teams or organizations that require more autonomy and customization. It's perfect for projects that need to be self-hosted, have specific infrastructure requirements, or require more control over data and deployment.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Netlify site using the Netlify CLI or the web interface.
2. Set up a new Coolify instance on your preferred server or cloud provider.
3. Import your exported site into Coolify using the Coolify import tool.
4. Configure any necessary settings, such as environment variables or Docker containers.
5. Test and deploy your site to ensure a smooth transition.

## Our Take
Coolify is still a relatively new player in the market, and while it shows great promise, it may not be production-ready for most users right now. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Coolify currently lacks built-in support for serverless functions, which may be a deal-breaker for some users. However, for teams that value self-hosting, customization, and control over their infrastructure, Coolify is definitely worth considering, and we recommend switching from Netlify if you don't require serverless functions or have a large team with complex infrastructure needs.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 members) that don't need serverless functions
* Medium-sized teams (10-50 members) that require self-hosting and customization
* Large teams (more than 50 members) with complex infrastructure needs
* Organizations with strict data ownership and compliance requirements
* Developers who prioritize autonomy and control over their infrastructure

## FAQ
### Is Coolify completely free?
Yes, Coolify is completely free and self-hosted, with no costs or licensing fees.
### Can I use Coolify with my existing Netlify site?
Yes, you can export your Netlify site and import it into Coolify, but you may need to configure some settings manually.
### Does Coolify support serverless functions?
Not yet, but the Coolify team is working on adding this feature in the near future.
### Is Coolify suitable for small projects?
Yes, Coolify is suitable for small projects, but it may require more technical expertise to set up and configure.
### Can I use Coolify with my favorite cloud provider?
Yes, Coolify supports most popular cloud providers, including AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure.

# Shopify vs WooCommerce (2026)

## Overview
Shopify and WooCommerce are two popular e-commerce platforms that enable businesses to create online stores and sell products. This comparison is beneficial for entrepreneurs, small businesses, and large enterprises looking to switch from one platform to another, primarily due to scalability, cost, or data ownership concerns. The core use case for both tools is to provide a comprehensive e-commerce solution, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their online store or reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Shopify offers a range of pricing plans, while WooCommerce is free to download and use, with costs limited to hosting and extensions.
* Data ownership: WooCommerce provides users with full ownership and control over their data, whereas Shopify stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Shopify is generally easier to set up and use, especially for those without extensive technical expertise, while WooCommerce requires more technical knowledge.
* Scalability: Both platforms can handle large volumes of traffic and sales, but WooCommerce's scalability is more dependent on the user's hosting and configuration.
* Payment gateway integration: Shopify has a more extensive range of built-in payment gateways, while WooCommerce relies on third-party extensions for additional payment options.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Shopify | WooCommerce |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $29-$299+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $29-$299+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $299+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Shopify:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Wide range of built-in features and integrations
* Reliable hosting and security
* Good customer support
* Limited customization options
**WooCommerce:**
* High degree of customization and control
* Free to download and use
* Large community of developers and users
* Scalable and flexible
* Requires technical expertise to set up and use

## When to Choose Each
Shopify is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses that want a hassle-free e-commerce solution with a wide range of built-in features and integrations. It is ideal for teams with limited technical expertise and a focus on ease of use. On the other hand, WooCommerce is suitable for larger enterprises or businesses that require a high degree of customization and control over their online store. It is ideal for teams with technical expertise and a focus on scalability and flexibility.

## Migration Path
1. Export your products, customers, and orders from Shopify using the built-in export feature, which provides a CSV file.
2. Install WooCommerce and the necessary extensions on your self-hosted WordPress site.
3. Use the WooCommerce import tool to import your products, customers, and orders from the CSV file.
4. Configure your payment gateways, shipping options, and other settings in WooCommerce.
5. Test your store to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
WooCommerce is a production-ready e-commerce platform for most users, offering a high degree of customization and control. However, one technical limitation worth knowing is that WooCommerce requires a good understanding of WordPress and PHP to fully utilize its features. For businesses that value flexibility and scalability, WooCommerce is a good choice, but for those who prioritize ease of use and a hassle-free experience, Shopify may be a better option.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with limited technical expertise that want more control over their online store
* Medium-sized enterprises that require a high degree of customization and scalability
* Large businesses with in-house development teams that want to reduce costs and increase flexibility
* E-commerce entrepreneurs who want to start small and scale up quickly without incurring high costs
* Businesses that do not need advanced features like point-of-sale integration or multi-channel selling

## FAQ
### Can I use WooCommerce with any theme?
Yes, WooCommerce can be used with any WordPress theme, but some themes are optimized for WooCommerce and provide better integration and design.

### Is Shopify more secure than WooCommerce?
Shopify provides reliable hosting and security, but WooCommerce can be just as secure if properly configured and maintained.

### Can I migrate my Shopify store to WooCommerce?
Yes, you can migrate your Shopify store to WooCommerce using the export and import features provided by both platforms.

### Does WooCommerce have built-in payment gateways?
No, WooCommerce relies on third-party extensions for payment gateways, but it has a wide range of options available.

### Is WooCommerce free?
Yes, WooCommerce is free to download and use, but you will need to pay for hosting and any additional extensions or themes you want to use.

## Overview

Leading small business accounting software from Intuit. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Akaunting is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: QuickBooks costs $30-$200+/month; Akaunting is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: QuickBooks is Proprietary; Akaunting is GPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: Akaunting can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Akaunting eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Akaunting has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

| Aspect | QuickBooks | Akaunting |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $30-$200+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$1,500/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$6,000/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### QuickBooks

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Akaunting

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [akaunting/akaunting](https://github.com/akaunting/akaunting) * ~8k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose QuickBooks if:** QuickBooks is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Akaunting if:** Akaunting is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from QuickBooks in its standard export format, review Akaunting import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Akaunting is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid QuickBooks tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Akaunting instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on QuickBooks until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated QuickBooks paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

### Is Akaunting free to use?
Yes. Akaunting is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from QuickBooks to Akaunting?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your QuickBooks data, follow the Akaunting import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Akaunting get regular updates?
Yes. Akaunting has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Akaunting without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.
